summary: Verified iter80 fire-and-forget race fix in services/supabase_sync.py (per-entity asyncio.Lock keyed by '{entity}:{entity_id}'). All 3 iter80 regression tests pass (cascade delete, iter74 no-orphan re-run, active B2C mirror health). Added new iter81 sanity test that reproduces the exact race with rapid POST->PUT->DELETE on unique slugs (single + 3-cycle batch) — both pass. 5/5 backend tests green in 81s.

minor.issue: Unbounded dict growth over app lifetime — a lock is added per unique (entity, id) touched and never evicted. For a shop with thousands of products this is fine but should be capped or LRU-evicted in future if entity_id cardinality grows (e.g. per-order writes).

critical_code_review_comments: Lock cleanup: _entity_locks never releases keys. Consider periodic pruning of unlocked entries or a bounded LRU to avoid slow memory creep in long-lived processes.

Race sanity test required ~5-6s of settle time (initial 3s was too short) because each cycle enqueues 3 upserts (b2c + 2 b2b) + 3 deletes serialized behind Supabase network I/O. This is expected under FIFO lock — not a regression.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter80 race fix is fully verified. Per-entity FIFO lock in supabase_sync._run correctly serializes upsert/delete on same (entity, entity_id). New regression test /app/backend/tests/test_iter81_race_sanity.py covers rapid POST->PUT->DELETE. Use sync psycopg2 for Supabase verification; wait >=5s after DELETE for fire-and-forget serialized chain to settle.
rca of the issue: Root cause (iter80): supabase_sync._run scheduled work via asyncio.create_task without ordering guarantees between tasks operating on the same product_id. A DELETE task could complete before the preceding PUT upsert task, causing the upsert to re-materialize a row after deletion. Fix: added module-level dict _entity_locks; _run now acquires asyncio.Lock keyed by f'{entity}:{entity_id}' before performing work, guaranteeing FIFO serialization. Verified by tests iter74/iter80/iter81 all green.
